title: Starter Journey — hero system, progressive stage diagrams, and modular step tiles
creator: Maya Ortega
description: Goal: Deliver a compact, composable visual system for the Starter Journey landing page that reduces cognitive load for first-run users and supports automated screenshot captures for release notes. Deliverables: hero artwork (static + Lottie fallback), 3 progressive stage diagrams (overview, hands-on, success), 6 modular step tiles (responsive variants), and a screenshot pipeline checklist for engineering. Constraints: must reuse existing color tokens and illustration library where possible, SVG-first assets for scaling, and accessible contrast >= 4.5:1 for critical text. Target metrics: +10% completion on first session 'Start' CTA in experiment, reduce help article opens from onboarding by 8%.
acceptance_criteria: Hero art delivered as 3x SVG variants (desktop/tablet/mobile) and Lottie JSON for animated header
Stage diagrams exported as optimized SVG and PNG at 2x for screenshots
Step tiles implemented as modular components with spec for spacing, type, and iconography
All text strings match copy in PRD and pass accessibility color/contrast checks
Screenshot checklist completed and verified in staging with automated capture script (see dev tasks)
mockups: Figma pages: Hero System / Stage Diagrams / Step Tiles
design_notes: Use existing illustration token set 'RedwoodLine' for stroke icons to keep file size small
Hero copy should be editable layers, avoid flattening text to allow rapid copy experiments
Animate only subtle entrance (fade+translateY) for Lottie variant to avoid distracting users
Provide a non-animated SVG fallback with identical visual hierarchy for low-power devices
Create a locked export grid for screenshots to ensure consistent cropping across breakpoints
dev_tasks: ENG-4812: screenshot capture pipeline (staging) - needs CSS hooks for hero state
ENG-4933: implement step-tile component and token mapping

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Lottie animation increases mobile CPU usage. Mitigation: provide reduced-motion SVG and toggle animation only for high-performance devices.
Risk: Copy changes near M1 could require re-export. Mitigation: build editable text layers and maintain a single source Figma file for quick iterates.
Risk: Screenshot inconsistency across browsers. Mitigation: locked export grid + dev verification step in ENG-4812.
